functions.name: Add-ADTEdgeExtension
functions.synopsis: Adds an extension for Microsoft Edge using the ExtensionSettings policy.
functions.description:
This function adds an extension for Microsoft Edge using the ExtensionSettings policy: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-manage-extensions-ref-guide.

This enables Edge Extensions to be installed and managed like applications, enabling extensions to be pushed to specific devices or users alongside existing GPO/Intune extension policies.

This should not be used in conjunction with Edge Management Service which leverages the same registry key to configure Edge extensions.

parameters.name: ExtensionID
parameters.description: The ID of the extension to add.

parameters.name: UpdateUrl
parameters.description: The update URL of the extension. This is the URL where the extension will check for updates.

parameters.name: InstallationMode
parameters.description: The installation mode of the extension. Allowed values: blocked, allowed, removed, force_installed, normal_installed.

parameters.name: MinimumVersionRequired
parameters.description: The minimum version of the extension required for installation.

examples:
Add-ADTEdgeExtension -ExtensionID "extensionID" -InstallationMode "force_installed" -UpdateUrl "https://edge.microsoft.com/extensionwebstorebase/v1/crx"

This example adds the specified extension to be force installed in Microsoft Edge.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return any output.

The `Add-ADTFont` function installs font files to the system by copying them to the Windows Fonts directory, registering them with the system, and creating the appropriate registry entry(s).

Supports .ttf, .ttc, and .otf file types.

parameters.name: Path

examples:

Installs the MyFont.ttf font file.

Add-ADTFont -Path "$($adtSession.DirFiles)\Fonts" -Recurse

Installs all font files in the Fonts directory and its subdirectories.

functions.name: Add-ADTModuleCallback
functions.synopsis: Adds a callback function to the nominated hooking point.
functions.description: This function adds a specified callback function to the nominated hooking point.

parameters.name: Hookpoint
parameters.description: Where you wish for the callback to be executed at. Valid hookpoints are: * OnInit (The callback is executed before the module is initialized) * OnStart (The callback is executed before the first deployment session is opened) * PreOpen (The callback is executed before a deployment session is opened) * PostOpen (The callback is executed after a deployment session is opened) * PreClose (The callback is executed before the deployment session is closed) * PostClose (The callback is executed after the deployment session is closed) * OnFinish (The callback is executed before the last deployment session is closed) * OnExit (The callback is executed after the last deployment session is closed) Each hook point supports multiple callbacks, each invoked in the order they're added. To see a list all the registered callbacks in order, use `Get-ADTModuleCallback`.

parameters.name: Callback
parameters.description: The callback function to add to the nominated hooking point.

examples:
Add-ADTModuleCallback -Hookpoint PostOpen -Callback (Get-Command -Name 'MyCallbackFunction')

Adds the specified callback function to be invoked after a DeploymentSession has opened.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Block-ADTAppExecution
functions.synopsis: Block the execution of an application(s).
functions.description:
This function is called when you pass the -BlockExecution parameter to the Stop-RunningApplications function. It does the following:

1) Makes a copy of this script in a temporary directory on the local machine.
2) Checks for an existing scheduled task from previous failed installation attempt where apps were blocked and if found, calls the Unblock-ADTAppExecution function to restore the original IFEO registry keys. This is to prevent the function from overriding the backup of the original IFEO options.
3) Creates a scheduled task to restore the IFEO registry key values in case the script is terminated uncleanly by calling `Unblock-ADTAppExecution` the local temporary copy of this module.
4) Modifies the "Image File Execution Options" registry key for the specified process(s) to call `Show-ADTInstallationPrompt` with the appropriate messaging via this module.
5) When the script is called with those parameters, it will display a custom message to the user to indicate that execution of the application has been blocked while the installation is in progress. The text of this message can be customized in the strings.psd1 file.

parameters.name: Processes
parameters.description: Name of the process or processes separated by commas.

parameters.name: WindowLocation
parameters.description: The location of the dialog on the screen.

examples:
Block-ADTAppExecution -Processes ('winword','excel')

This example blocks the execution of Microsoft Word and Excel.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Copy-ADTFile
functions.synopsis: Copies files and directories from a source to a destination.
functions.description: Copies files and directories from a source to a destination. This function supports recursive copying, overwriting existing files, and returning the copied items.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Path of the file to copy. Multiple paths can be specified.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: Destination Path of the file to copy.

parameters.name: Recurse
parameters.description: Copy files in subdirectories.

parameters.name: Flatten
parameters.description: Flattens the files into the root destination directory.

parameters.name: ContinueFileCopyOnError
parameters.description: Continue copying files if an error is encountered. This will continue the deployment script and will warn about files that failed to be copied.

parameters.name: FileCopyMode
parameters.description: Select from 'Native' or 'Robocopy'. Default is configured in config.psd1. Note that Robocopy supports * in file names, but not folders, in source paths.

parameters.name: RobocopyParams
parameters.description: Override the default Robocopy parameters.

parameters.name: RobocopyAdditionalParams
parameters.description: Append to the default Robocopy parameters.

examples:
Copy-ADTFile -Path 'C:\Path\file.txt' -Destination 'D:\Destination\file.txt'

Copies the file 'file.txt' from 'C:\Path' to 'D:\Destination'.

Copy-ADTFile -Path 'C:\Path\Folder' -Destination 'D:\Destination\Folder' -Recurse

Recursively copies the folder 'Folder' from 'C:\Path' to 'D:\Destination'.

Copy-ADTFile -Path 'C:\Path\file.txt' -Destination 'D:\Destination\file.txt'

Copies the file 'file.txt' from 'C:\Path' to 'D:\Destination', overwriting the destination file if it exists.

Copy-ADTFile -Path "$($adtSession.DirFiles)\*" -Destination C:\some\random\file\path

Copies all files within the active session's Files folder to 'C:\some\random\file\path', overwriting the destination file if it exists.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The path of the file or folder to copy.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: The path of the destination folder to append to the root of the user profile.

parameters.name: BasePath
parameters.description: The base path to append the destination folder to.

parameters.name: Recurse
parameters.description: Copy files in subdirectories.

parameters.name: Flatten
parameters.description: Flattens the files into the root destination directory.

parameters.name: ContinueFileCopyOnError
parameters.description: Continue copying files if an error is encountered. This will continue the deployment script and will warn about files that failed to be copied.

parameters.name: FileCopyMode
parameters.description: Select from 'Native' or 'Robocopy'. Default is configured in config.psd1. Note that Robocopy supports * in file names, but not folders, in source paths.

parameters.name: RobocopyParams
parameters.description: Override the default Robocopy parameters.

parameters.name: RobocopyAdditionalParams
parameters.description: Append to the default Robocopy parameters.

parameters.name: UserProfiles
parameters.description: Specifies one or more UserProfile objects to copy files into.

parameters.name: ExcludeNTAccount
parameters.description: Specify NT account names in Domain\Username format to exclude from the list of user profiles.

parameters.name: IncludeSystemProfiles
parameters.description: Include system profiles: SYSTEM, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE.

parameters.name: IncludeServiceProfiles
parameters.description: Include service profiles where NTAccount begins with NT SERVICE.

parameters.name: ExcludeDefaultUser
parameters.description: Exclude the Default User.

examples:
Copy-ADTFileToUserProfiles -Path "$($adtSession.DirSupportFiles)\config.txt" -Destination "AppData\Roaming\MyApp"

Copy a single file to C:\Users\<UserName>\AppData\Roaming\MyApp for each user.

Copy-ADTFileToUserProfiles -Path "$($adtSession.DirSupportFiles)\config.txt","$($adtSession.DirSupportFiles)\config2.txt" -Destination "AppData\Roaming\MyApp"

Copy two files to C:\Users\<UserName>\AppData\Roaming\MyApp for each user.

Copy-ADTFileToUserProfiles -Path "$($adtSession.DirFiles)\MyDocs" Destination "MyApp" -BasePath "Documents" -Recurse

Copy an entire folder recursively to a new MyApp folder under each user's Documents folder.

Copy-ADTFileToUserProfiles -Path "$($adtSession.DirFiles)\.appConfigFolder" -Recurse

Copy an entire folder to C:\Users\<UserName> for each user.

functions.name: Get-ADTApplication
functions.synopsis: Retrieves information about installed applications.
functions.description: Retrieves information about installed applications by querying the registry. You can specify an application name, a product code, or both. Returns information about application publisher, name & version, product code, uninstall string, install source, location, date, and application architecture.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: The name of the application to retrieve information for. Performs a contains match on the application display name by default.

parameters.name: NameMatch
parameters.description: Specifies the type of match to perform on the application name. Valid values are 'Contains', 'Exact', 'Wildcard', and 'Regex'. The default value is 'Contains'.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: The product code of the application to retrieve information for.

parameters.name: ApplicationType
parameters.description: Specifies the type of application to remove. Valid values are 'All', 'MSI', and 'EXE'. The default value is 'All'.

parameters.name: IncludeUpdatesAndHotfixes
parameters.description: Include matches against updates and hotfixes in results.

parameters.name: FilterScript
parameters.description: A script used to filter the results as they're processed.

examples:
Get-ADTApplication

This example retrieves information about all installed applications.

Get-ADTApplication -Name 'Acrobat'

Returns all applications that contain the name 'Acrobat' in the DisplayName.

Get-ADTApplication -Name 'Adobe Acrobat Reader' -NameMatch 'Exact'

Returns all applications that match the name 'Adobe Acrobat Reader' exactly.

Get-ADTApplication -ProductCode '{AC76BA86-7AD7-1033-7B44-AC0F074E4100}'

Returns the application with the specified ProductCode.

Get-ADTApplication -Name 'Acrobat' -ApplicationType 'MSI' -FilterScript { $_.Publisher -match 'Adobe' }

Returns all MSI applications that contain the name 'Acrobat' in the DisplayName and 'Adobe' in the Publisher name.

parameters.name: Parameters

parameters.description: Argument to pass to the method being executed. Allows execution of method by using named parameters.

examples:
PS C:\>$ShellApp = New-Object -ComObject 'Shell.Application'
PS C:\>$null = Invoke-ADTObjectMethod -InputObject $ShellApp -MethodName 'MinimizeAll'

Minimizes all windows.
functions.outputs: System.Object The object returned by the method being invoked.

functions.name: Invoke-ADTRegSvr32
functions.synopsis: Register or unregister a DLL file.
functions.description: Register or unregister a DLL file using regsvr32.exe. This function determines the bitness of the DLL file and uses the appropriate version of regsvr32.exe to perform the action. It supports both 32-bit and 64-bit DLL files on corresponding operating systems.

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.description: Path to the DLL file.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Specify whether to register or unregister the DLL.

examples:
Invoke-ADTRegSvr32 -FilePath "C:\Test\DcTLSFileToDMSComp.dll" -Action 'Register'

Registers the specified DLL file.

Invoke-ADTRegSvr32 -FilePath "C:\Test\DcTLSFileToDMSComp.dll" -Action 'Unregister'

Unregisters the specified DLL file.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return objects.

functions.name: Invoke-ADTSCCMTask
functions.synopsis: Triggers SCCM to invoke the requested schedule task ID.
functions.description: Triggers SCCM to invoke the requested schedule task ID. This function supports a variety of Schedule Id values as defined via https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configmgr/develop/reference/core/clients/client-classes/triggerschedule-method-in-class-sms_client.

parameters.name: ScheduleId
parameters.description: Name of the Schedule Id to trigger.

examples:
Invoke-ADTSCCMTask -ScheduleId 'SoftwareUpdatesScan'

Triggers the 'SoftwareUpdatesScan' schedule task in SCCM.

Invoke-ADTSCCMTask -ScheduleId 'HardwareInventory'

Triggers the 'HardwareInventory' schedule task in SCCM.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return any objects.

functions.name: Mount-ADTWimFile
functions.synopsis: Mounts a WIM file to a specified directory.
functions.description: Mounts a WIM file to a specified directory. The function supports mounting by image index or image name. It also provides options to forcefully remove existing directories and return the mounted image details.

parameters.name: ImagePath
parameters.description: Path to the WIM file to be mounted.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Directory where the WIM file will be mounted. The directory either must not exist, or must be empty and not have a pre-existing WIM mounted.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: Index of the image within the WIM file to be mounted.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Name of the image within the WIM file to be mounted.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Forces the removal of the existing directory if it is not empty.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: If specified, the function will return the results from `Mount-WindowsImage`.

examples:
Mount-ADTWimFile -ImagePath 'C:\Images\install.wim' -Path 'C:\Mount' -Index 1

Mounts the first image in the 'install.wim' file to the 'C:\Mount' directory, creating the directory if it does not exist.

Mount-ADTWimFile -ImagePath 'C:\Images\install.wim' -Path 'C:\Mount' -Name 'Windows 10 Pro'

Mounts the image named 'Windows 10 Pro' in the 'install.wim' file to the 'C:\Mount' directory, creating the directory if it does not exist.

Mount-ADTWimFile -ImagePath 'C:\Images\install.wim' -Path 'C:\Mount' -Index 1 -Force

Mounts the first image in the 'install.wim' file to the 'C:\Mount' directory, forcefully removing the existing directory if it is not empty.
functions.outputs: Microsoft.Dism.Commands.ImageObject Returns the mounted image details if the PassThru parameter is specified.

functions.name: New-ADTErrorRecord
functions.synopsis: Creates a new ErrorRecord object.
functions.description: This function creates a new ErrorRecord object with the specified exception, error category, and optional parameters. It allows for detailed error information to be captured and returned to the caller, who can then throw the error.

parameters.name: Exception
parameters.description: The exception object that caused the error.

parameters.name: Category
parameters.description: The category of the error.

parameters.name: ErrorId
parameters.description: The identifier for the error. Default is 'NotSpecified'.

parameters.name: TargetObject
parameters.description: The target object that the error is related to.

parameters.name: TargetName
parameters.description: The name of the target that the error is related to.

parameters.name: TargetType
parameters.description: The type of the target that the error is related to.

parameters.name: Activity
parameters.description: The activity that was being performed when the error occurred.

parameters.name: Reason
parameters.description: The reason for the error.

parameters.name: RecommendedAction
parameters.description: The recommended action to resolve the error.

examples:
PS C:\>$exception = [System.Exception]::new("An error occurred.")
PS C:\>$category = [System.Management.Automation.ErrorCategory]::NotSpecified
PS C:\>New-ADTErrorRecord -Exception $exception -Category $category -ErrorId "CustomErrorId" -TargetObject $null -TargetName "TargetName" -TargetType "TargetType" -Activity "Activity" -Reason "Reason" -RecommendedAction "RecommendedAction"

Creates a new ErrorRecord object with the specified parameters.
functions.outputs: System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord This function returns an ErrorRecord object.

functions.name: New-ADTFolder
functions.synopsis: Create a new folder.
functions.description: Create a new folder if it does not exist. This function checks if the specified path already exists and creates the folder if it does not. It logs the creation process and handles any errors that may occur during the folder creation.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: Path to the new folder to create.

examples:
New-ADTFolder -LiteralPath "$env:WinDir\System32"

Creates a new folder at the specified path if it does not already exist.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: New-ADTLogFileName
functions.synopsis: Generates a new log file name based off the current deployment session's properties.
functions.description: The `New-ADTLogFileName` function generates a new log file name based off the current deployment session's properties, using the same default format that PSAppDeployToolkit uses itself.

parameters.name: Discriminator
parameters.description: The identifier to pre-format the log file name with.

parameters.name: FileNameOnly
parameters.description: If specified, just returns a log file name without any preceding path.

examples:
New-ADTLogFileName -Discriminator Setup

This example returns a pre-formatted string that can be used as a log file name.
functions.outputs: System.String Returns a pre-formatted string with the specified discriminator.

functions.name: New-ADTMsiTransform
functions.synopsis: Create a transform file for an MSI database.
functions.description: Create a transform file for an MSI database and create/modify properties in the Properties table. This function allows you to specify an existing transform to apply before making changes and to define the path for the new transform file. If the new transform file already exists, it will be deleted before creating a new one.

parameters.name: MsiPath
parameters.description: Specify the path to an MSI file.

parameters.name: ApplyTransformPath
parameters.description: Specify the path to a transform which should be applied to the MSI database before any new properties are created or modified.

parameters.name: NewTransformPath
parameters.description: Specify the path where the new transform file with the desired properties will be created. If a transform file of the same name already exists, it will be deleted before a new one is created.

parameters.name: TransformProperties
parameters.description: Hashtable which contains calls to `Set-ADTMsiProperty` for configuring the desired properties which should be included in the new transform file. Example hashtable: `@{ ALLUSERS = 1 }`

examples:
New-ADTMsiTransform -MsiPath 'C:\Temp\PSADTInstall.msi' -TransformProperties @{
ALLUSERS = 1
AgreeToLicense = 'Yes'
REBOOT = 'ReallySuppress'
RebootYesNo = 'No'
ROOTDRIVE = 'C:'
}

Creates a new transform file for the specified MSI with the given properties.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: New-ADTShortcut
functions.synopsis: Creates a new .lnk or .url type shortcut.
functions.description: Creates a new shortcut .lnk or .url file, with configurable options. This function allows you to specify various parameters such as the target path, arguments, icon location, description, working directory, window style, run as administrator, and hotkey.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: Path to save the shortcut.

parameters.name: TargetPath
parameters.description: Target path or URL that the shortcut launches.

parameters.name: Arguments
parameters.description: Arguments to be passed to the target path.

parameters.name: IconLocation
parameters.description: Location of the icon used for the shortcut.

parameters.name: IconIndex
parameters.description: The index of the icon. Executables, DLLs, ICO files with multiple icons need the icon index to be specified. This parameter is an Integer. The first index is 0.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Description of the shortcut.

parameters.name: WorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Working Directory to be used for the target path.

parameters.name: WindowStyle
parameters.description: Windows style of the application. Options: Normal, Maximized, Minimized.

parameters.name: RunAsAdmin
parameters.description: Set shortcut to run program as administrator. This option will prompt user to elevate when executing shortcut.

parameters.name: Hotkey
parameters.description: Create a Hotkey to launch the shortcut, e.g. "CTRL+SHIFT+F".

examples:
New-ADTShortcut -LiteralPath "$envCommonStartMenuPrograms\My Shortcut.lnk" -TargetPath "$envWinDir\notepad.exe" -IconLocation "$envWinDir\notepad.exe" -Description 'Notepad' -WorkingDirectory '%HOMEDRIVE%\%HOMEPATH%'

Creates a new shortcut for Notepad with the specified parameters.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return any output.

functions.name: New-ADTTemplate
functions.synopsis: Creates a new folder containing a template front end and module folder, ready to customise.
functions.description: Specify a destination path where a new folder will be created. You also have the option of creating a template for v3 compatibility mode.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: Path where the new folder should be created. Default is the current working directory.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Name of the newly created folder. Default is PSAppDeployToolkit_Version.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.description: Defaults to 4 for the standard v4 template. Use 3 for the v3 compatibility mode template.

parameters.name: Show
parameters.description: Opens the newly created folder in Windows Explorer.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: If the destination folder already exists, this switch will force the creation of the new folder.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Returns the newly created folder object.

examples:
New-ADTTemplate -Destination 'C:\Temp' -Name 'PSAppDeployToolkitv4'

Creates a new v4 template named PSAppDeployToolkitv4 under C:\Temp.

New-ADTTemplate -Destination 'C:\Temp' -Name 'PSAppDeployToolkitv3' -Version 3

Creates a new v3 compatibility mode template named PSAppDeployToolkitv3 under C:\Temp.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: New-ADTValidateScriptErrorRecord
functions.synopsis: Creates a new ErrorRecord for script validation errors.
functions.description: This function creates a new ErrorRecord object for script validation errors. It takes the parameter name, provided value, exception message, and an optional inner exception to build a detailed error record. This helps in identifying and handling invalid parameter values in scripts.

parameters.name: ParameterName
parameters.description: The name of the parameter that caused the validation error.

parameters.name: ProvidedValue
parameters.description: The value provided for the parameter that caused the validation error.

parameters.name: ExceptionMessage
parameters.description: The message describing the validation error.

parameters.name: InnerException
parameters.description: An optional inner exception that provides more details about the validation error.

examples:
PS C:\>$paramName = "FilePath"
PS C:\>$providedValue = "C:\InvalidPath"
PS C:\>$exceptionMessage = "The specified path does not exist."
PS C:\>New-ADTValidateScriptErrorRecord -ParameterName $paramName -ProvidedValue $providedValue -ExceptionMessage $exceptionMessage

Creates a new ErrorRecord for a validation error with the specified parameters.
functions.outputs: System.Management.Automation.ErrorRecord This function returns an ErrorRecord object.

functions.name: New-ADTZipFile
functions.synopsis: Create a new zip archive or add content to an existing archive.
functions.description: Create a new zip archive or add content to an existing archive by using PowerShell's Compress-Archive.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: One or more paths to compress. Supports wildcards.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: One or more literal paths to compress.

parameters.name: DestinationPath
parameters.description: The file path for where the zip file should be created.

parameters.name: CompressionLevel
parameters.description: The level of compression to apply to the zip file.

parameters.name: Update
parameters.description: Specifies whether to update an existing zip file or not.

parameters.name: Force
parameters.description: Specifies whether an existing zip file should be overwritten.

parameters.name: RemoveSourceAfterArchiving
parameters.description: Remove the source path after successfully archiving the content.

examples: New-ADTZipFile -SourceDirectory 'E:\Testing\Logs' -DestinationPath 'E:\Testing\TestingLogs.zip'
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Open-ADTSession
functions.synopsis: Opens a new ADT session.
functions.description: This function initializes and opens a new ADT session with the specified parameters. It handles the setup of the session environment and processes any callbacks defined for the session. If the session fails to open, it handles the error and closes the session if necessary.

parameters.name: SessionState
parameters.description: Defaults to $PSCmdlet.SessionState to get the caller's SessionState, so only required if you need to override this.

parameters.name: DeploymentType
parameters.description: Specifies the type of deployment: Install, Uninstall, or Repair.

parameters.name: DeployMode
parameters.description: Specifies the deployment mode: Interactive, NonInteractive, or Silent.

parameters.name: SuppressRebootPassThru
parameters.description: Suppresses reboot pass-through.

parameters.name: TerminalServerMode
parameters.description: Enables Terminal Server mode.

parameters.name: DisableLogging
parameters.description: Disables logging for the session.

parameters.name: AppVendor
parameters.description: Specifies the application vendor.

parameters.name: AppName
parameters.description: Specifies the application name.

parameters.name: AppVersion
parameters.description: Specifies the application version.

parameters.name: AppArch
parameters.description: Specifies the application architecture.

parameters.name: AppLang
parameters.description: Specifies the application language.

parameters.name: AppRevision
parameters.description: Specifies the application revision.

parameters.name: AppScriptVersion
parameters.description: Specifies the application script version.

parameters.name: AppScriptDate
parameters.description: Specifies the application script date.

parameters.name: AppScriptAuthor
parameters.description: Specifies the application script author.

parameters.name: InstallName
parameters.description: Specifies the install name.

parameters.name: InstallTitle
parameters.description: Specifies the install title.

parameters.name: DeployAppScriptFriendlyName
parameters.description: Specifies the friendly name of the deploy application script.

parameters.name: DeployAppScriptVersion
parameters.description: Specifies the version of the deploy application script.

parameters.name: DeployAppScriptParameters
parameters.description: Specifies the parameters for the deploy application script.

parameters.name: AppSuccessExitCodes
parameters.description: Specifies the application exit codes.

parameters.name: AppRebootExitCodes
parameters.description: Specifies the application reboot codes.

parameters.name: AppProcessesToClose
parameters.description: Specifies one or more processes that require closing to ensure a successful deployment.

parameters.name: RequireAdmin
parameters.description: Specifies that this deployment requires administrative permissions.

parameters.name: ScriptDirectory
parameters.description: Specifies the base path for Files and SupportFiles.

parameters.name: DirFiles
parameters.description: Specifies the override path to Files.

parameters.name: DirSupportFiles
parameters.description: Specifies the override path to SupportFiles.

parameters.name: DefaultMsiFile
parameters.description: Specifies the default MSI file.

parameters.name: DefaultMstFile
parameters.description: Specifies the default MST file.

parameters.name: DefaultMspFiles
parameters.description: Specifies the default MSP files.

parameters.name: DisableDefaultMsiProcessList
parameters.description: Specifies that the zero-config MSI code should not gather process names from the MSI file.

parameters.name: ForceMsiDetection
parameters.description: Specifies that MSI files should be detected and parsed during session initialization, irrespective of whether any App values are provided.

parameters.name: ForceWimDetection
parameters.description: Specifies that WIM files should be detected and mounted during session initialization, irrespective of whether any App values are provided.

parameters.name: NoSessionDetection
parameters.description: When DeployMode is not specified or is Auto, bypasses DeployMode adjustment when there's no logged on user session available.

parameters.name: NoOobeDetection
parameters.description: When DeployMode is not specified or is Auto, bypasses DeployMode adjustment when the device hasn't completed the OOBE or a user ESP is active.

parameters.name: NoProcessDetection
parameters.description: When DeployMode is not specified or is Auto, bypasses DeployMode adjustment when there's no processes to close in the specified AppProcessesToClose list.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Passes the session object through the pipeline.

parameters.name: LogName
parameters.description: Specifies an override for the default-generated log file name.

parameters.name: SessionClass
parameters.description: Specifies an override for PSADT.Module.DeploymentSession class. Use this if you're deriving a class inheriting off PSAppDeployToolkit's base.

parameters.name: UnboundArguments
parameters.description: Captures any additional arguments passed to the function.

examples:
Open-ADTSession -SessionState $ExecutionContext.SessionState -DeploymentType "Install" -DeployMode "Interactive"

Opens a new ADT session with the specified parameters.
functions.outputs: ADTSession This function returns the session object if -PassThru is specified.

functions.name: Out-ADTPowerShellEncodedCommand
functions.synopsis: Encodes a PowerShell command into a Base64 string.
functions.description: This function takes a PowerShell command as input and encodes it into a Base64 string. This is useful for passing commands to PowerShell through mechanisms that require encoded input.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: The PowerShell command to be encoded.

examples:
Out-ADTPowerShellEncodedCommand -Command 'Get-Process'

Encodes the "Get-Process" command into a Base64 string.
functions.outputs: System.String This function returns the encoded Base64 string representation of the input command.

functions.name: Register-ADTDll
functions.synopsis: Register a DLL file.
functions.description: This function registers a DLL file using regsvr32.exe. It ensures that the specified DLL file exists before attempting to register it. If the file does not exist, it throws an error.

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.description: Path to the DLL file.

examples:
Register-ADTDll -FilePath "C:\Test\DcTLSFileToDMSComp.dll"

Registers the specified DLL file.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return objects.

functions.name: Remove-ADTContentFromCache
functions.synopsis: Removes the toolkit content from the cache folder on the local machine and reverts the $adtSession.DirFiles and $adtSession.SupportFiles directory.
functions.description: This function removes the toolkit content from the cache folder on the local machine. It also reverts the $adtSession.DirFiles and $adtSession.SupportFiles directory to their original state. If the specified cache folder does not exist, it logs a message and exits.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: The path to the software cache folder.

examples:
Remove-ADTContentFromCache -LiteralPath "$envWinDir\Temp\PSAppDeployToolkit"

Removes the toolkit content from the specified cache folder.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return objects.

functions.name: Remove-ADTDesktopShortcut
functions.synopsis: Removes desktop shortcuts from the common desktop folder or logged on user's desktop.
functions.description: The `Remove-ADTDesktopShortcut` function removes desktop shortcuts from the common desktop folder or logged on user's desktop, either all since the commencement of the session, all shortcuts in general, or based on a custom FilterScript.

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.description: The scope of which desktop directory to target. Valid values for this parameter are: - `AllUsersDesktop`: Removes shortcuts from the common desktop (`$EnvCommonDesktop`). - `RunAsActiveUser`: Removes shortcuts from the active user's desktop.

parameters.name: SinceSessionStart
parameters.description: Removes all shortcuts created after the active deployment session commenced.

parameters.name: RemoveAllShortcuts
parameters.description: Removes all shortcuts in the nominated scope(s).

parameters.name: FilterScript
parameters.description: Removes all shortcuts that match the given FilterScript (filtration on any FileInfo property/method is available).

examples:
Remove-ADTDesktopShortcut -SinceSessionStart

This example removes all shortcuts created after the active deployment session started from the common desktop folder.
functions.outputs: None This function returns no output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTEdgeExtension
functions.synopsis: Removes an extension for Microsoft Edge using the ExtensionSettings policy.
functions.description:
This function removes an extension for Microsoft Edge using the ExtensionSettings policy: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-manage-extensions-ref-guide.

This enables Edge Extensions to be installed and managed like applications, enabling extensions to be pushed to specific devices or users alongside existing GPO/Intune extension policies.

This should not be used in conjunction with Edge Management Service which leverages the same registry key to configure Edge extensions.

parameters.name: ExtensionID
parameters.description: The ID of the extension to remove.

examples:
Remove-ADTEdgeExtension -ExtensionID "extensionID"

Removes the specified extension from Microsoft Edge.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return objects.

functions.name: Remove-ADTEnvironmentVariable
functions.synopsis: Removes the specified environment variable.
functions.description: This function removes the specified environment variable.

parameters.name: Variable
parameters.description: The variable to remove.

parameters.name: Target
parameters.description: The target of the variable to remove. This can be the machine, user, or process.

examples:
Remove-ADTEnvironmentVariable -Variable Path

Removes the Path environment variable.

Remove-ADTEnvironmentVariable -Variable Path -Target Machine

Removes the Path environment variable for the machine.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTFile
functions.synopsis: Removes one or more items from a given path on the filesystem.
functions.description: This function removes one or more items from a given path on the filesystem. It can handle both wildcard paths and literal paths. If the specified path does not exist, it logs a warning instead of throwing an error. The function can also delete items recursively if the Recurse parameter is specified.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Specifies the file on the filesystem to be removed. The value of Path will accept wildcards. Will accept an array of values.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: Specifies the file on the filesystem to be removed. The value of LiteralPath is used exactly as it is typed; no characters are interpreted as wildcards. Will accept an array of values.

parameters.name: Recurse
parameters.description: Deletes the files in the specified location(s) and in all child items of the location(s).

examples:
Remove-ADTFile -LiteralPath 'C:\Windows\Downloaded Program Files\Temp.inf'

Removes the specified file.

Remove-ADTFile -LiteralPath 'C:\Windows\Downloaded Program Files' -Recurse

Removes the specified folder and all its contents recursively.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTFileFromUserProfiles
functions.synopsis: Removes one or more items from each user profile on the system.
functions.description: This function removes one or more items from each user profile on the system. It can handle both wildcard paths and literal paths. If the specified path does not exist, it logs a warning instead of throwing an error. The function can also delete items recursively if the Recurse parameter is specified. Additionally, it allows excluding specific NT accounts, system profiles, service profiles, and the default user profile.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Specifies the path to append to the root of the user profile to be resolved. The value of Path will accept wildcards. Will accept an array of values.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: Specifies the path to append to the root of the user profile to be resolved. The value of LiteralPath is used exactly as it is typed; no characters are interpreted as wildcards. Will accept an array of values.

parameters.name: Recurse
parameters.description: Deletes the files in the specified location(s) and in all child items of the location(s).

parameters.name: ExcludeNTAccount
parameters.description: Specify NT account names in Domain\Username format to exclude from the list of user profiles.

parameters.name: ExcludeDefaultUser
parameters.description: Exclude the Default User.

parameters.name: IncludeSystemProfiles
parameters.description: Include system profiles: SYSTEM, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE.

parameters.name: IncludeServiceProfiles
parameters.description: Include service profiles where NTAccount begins with NT SERVICE.

examples:
Remove-ADTFileFromUserProfiles -Path "AppData\Roaming\MyApp\config.txt"

Removes the specified file from each user profile on the system.

Remove-ADTFileFromUserProfiles -Path "AppData\Local\MyApp" -Recurse

Removes the specified folder and all its contents recursively from each user profile on the system.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTFolder
functions.synopsis: Remove folder and files if they exist.
functions.description: This function removes a folder and all files within it, with or without recursion, in a given path. If the specified folder does not exist, it logs a warning instead of throwing an error. The function can also delete items recursively if the DisableRecursion parameter is not specified.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: A path to the folder to remove. Can contain wildcards.

parameters.name: LiteralPath
parameters.description: A literal path to the folder to remove.

parameters.name: InputObject
parameters.description: A DirectoryInfo object to remove. Available for pipelining.

parameters.name: DisableRecursion
parameters.description: Disables recursion while deleting.

examples:
Remove-ADTFolder -Path "$envWinDir\Downloaded Program Files"

Deletes all files and subfolders in the Windows\Downloaded Program Files folder.

Remove-ADTFolder -Path "$envTemp\MyAppCache" -DisableRecursion

Deletes all files in the Temp\MyAppCache folder but does not delete any subfolders.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTFont
functions.synopsis: Removes a font from the system.
functions.description: The `Remove-ADTFont` removes a font from the system by removing the font resource, deleting the registry entry, and removing the file from the Windows Fonts directory.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: The name of the font file (e.g., 'arial.ttf') or the font name as it appears in the registry.

examples:
Remove-ADTFont -Name 'MyFont.ttf'

Removes the MyFont.ttf font.
functions.outputs: None This function does not generate any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTHashtableNullOrEmptyValues
functions.synopsis: Removes any key/value pairs from the supplied hashtable where the value is null.
functions.description: This function removes any key/value pairs from the supplied hashtable where the value is null.

parameters.name: Hashtable
parameters.description: The hashtable to remove null values from.

examples:
Remove-ADTHashtableNullOrEmptyValues -Hashtable

Returns a new hashtable with only key/values where the value isn't null.
functions.outputs: System.Collections.Hashtable Returns a new hashtable with only key/values where the value isn't null.

functions.name: Remove-ADTIniSection
functions.synopsis: Opens an INI file and removes the specified section.
functions.description: Opens an INI file and removes the specified section.

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.description: Path to the INI file.

parameters.name: Section
parameters.description: Section within the INI file.

examples:
Remove-ADTIniSection -FilePath "$env:ProgramFilesX86\IBM\Notes\notes.ini" -Section 'Notes'

Removes the 'Notes' section of the 'notes.ini' file.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTIniValue
functions.synopsis: Opens an INI file and removes the specified key or section.
functions.description: Opens an INI file and removes the specified key or section.

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.description: Path to the INI file.

parameters.name: Section
parameters.description: Section within the INI file.

parameters.name: Key
parameters.description: Key within the section of the INI file.

examples:
Remove-ADTIniValue -FilePath "$env:ProgramFilesX86\IBM\Notes\notes.ini" -Section 'Notes' -Key 'KeyFileName'

Removes the 'KeyFileName' key from the 'Notes' section of the 'notes.ini' file.

Remove-ADTIniValue -FilePath "$env:ProgramFilesX86\IBM\Notes\notes.ini" -Section 'Notes'

Removes the entire 'Notes' section of the 'notes.ini' file.
functions.outputs: None This function does not return any output.

functions.name: Remove-ADTInvalidFileNameChars
functions.synopsis: Remove invalid characters from the supplied string.
functions.description: This function removes invalid characters from the supplied string and returns a valid filename as a string. It ensures that the resulting string does not contain any characters that are not allowed in filenames. This function should not be used for entire paths as '\' is not a valid filename character.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Text to remove invalid filename characters from.

examples:

functions.name: Set-ADTActiveSetup
functions.synopsis: Creates an Active Setup entry in the registry to execute a file for each user upon login.
functions.description:
Active Setup allows handling of per-user changes registry/file changes upon login.

A registry key is created in the HKLM registry hive which gets replicated to the HKCU hive when a user logs in.

If the "Version" value of the Active Setup entry in HKLM is higher than the version value in HKCU, the file referenced in "StubPath" is executed.

This Function:

- Creates the registry entries in "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\$($adtSession.InstallName)".
- Creates StubPath value depending on the file extension of the $StubExePath parameter.
- Handles Version value with YYYYMMDDHHMMSS granularity to permit re-installs on the same day and still trigger Active Setup after Version increase.
- Copies/overwrites the StubPath file to $StubExePath destination path if file exists in 'Files' subdirectory of script directory.
- Executes the StubPath file for the current user based on $NoExecuteForCurrentUser (no need to logout/login to trigger Active Setup).

parameters.name: StubExePath
parameters.description: Use this parameter to specify the destination path of the file that will be executed upon user login. Note: Place the file you want users to execute in the '\Files' subdirectory of the script directory and the toolkit will install it to the path specificed in this parameter.

parameters.name: Arguments
parameters.description: Arguments to pass to the file being executed.

parameters.name: Wow6432Node
parameters.description: Specify this switch to use Active Setup entry under Wow6432Node on a 64-bit OS.

parameters.name: ExecutionPolicy
parameters.description: Specifies the ExecutionPolicy to set when StubExePath is a PowerShell script.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.description: Optional. Specify version for Active setup entry. Active Setup is not triggered if Version value has more than 8 consecutive digits. Use commas to get around this limitation. Note: - Do not use this parameter if it is not necessary. PSADT will handle this parameter automatically using the time of the installation as the version number. - In Windows 10, scripts and executables might be blocked by AppLocker. Ensure that the path given to -StubExePath will permit end users to run scripts and executables unelevated.

parameters.name: Locale
parameters.description: Optional. Arbitrary string used to specify the installation language of the file being executed. Not replicated to HKCU.

parameters.name: PurgeActiveSetupKey
parameters.description: Remove Active Setup entry from HKLM registry hive. Will also load each logon user's HKCU registry hive to remove Active Setup entry. Function returns after purging.

parameters.name: DisableActiveSetup
parameters.description: Disables the Active Setup entry so that the StubPath file will not be executed. This also enables -NoExecuteForCurrentUser.

parameters.name: NoExecuteForCurrentUser
parameters.description: Specifies whether the StubExePath should be executed for the current user. Since this user is already logged in, the user won't have the application started without logging out and logging back in.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Returns a ProcessResult from the execution of the ActiveSetup configuration for the current user if `-PassThru` is provided.

examples: Set-ADTActiveSetup -StubExePath 'C:\Users\Public\Company\ProgramUserConfig.vbs' -Arguments '/Silent' -Description 'Program User Config' -Key 'ProgramUserConfig' -Locale 'en'

Set-ADTActiveSetup -StubExePath "$envWinDir\regedit.exe" -Arguments "/S `"%SystemDrive%\Program Files (x86)\PS App Deploy\PSAppDeployHKCUSettings.reg`"" -Description 'PS App Deploy Config' -Key 'PS_App_Deploy_Config'

Delete "ProgramUserConfig" active setup entry from all registry hives.

functions.synopsis: Show a welcome dialog prompting the user with information about the deployment and actions to be performed before the deployment can begin.
functions.description:
The following prompts can be included in the welcome dialog:

* Close the specified running applications, or optionally close the applications without showing a prompt (using the `-Silent` switch).
* Defer the deployment a certain number of times, for a certain number of days or until a deadline is reached.
* Countdown until applications are automatically closed.
* Prevent users from launching the specified applications while the deployment is in progress.

functions.name: Start-ADTMsiProcess
functions.synopsis: Executes msiexec.exe to perform actions such as install, uninstall, patch, repair, or active setup for MSI and MSP files or MSI product codes.
functions.description:
This function utilizes msiexec.exe to handle various operations on MSI and MSP files, as well as MSI product codes. The operations include installation, uninstallation, patching, repair, and setting up active configurations.

If the -Action parameter is set to "Install" and the MSI is already installed, the function will terminate without performing any actions.

The function automatically sets default switches for msiexec based on preferences defined in the config.psd1 file. Additionally, it generates a log file name and creates a verbose log for all msiexec operations, ensuring detailed tracking.

The MSI or MSP file is expected to reside in the "Files" subdirectory of the App Deploy Toolkit, with transform files expected to be in the same directory as the MSI file.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Specifies the action to be performed. Available options: Install, Uninstall, Patch, Repair, ActiveSetup.

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.description: The file path to the MSI/MSP file. If the specified FilePath is just a file name, the function will look within `$adtSession.DirFiles` for the specified file, so long as a session is active.

parameters.name: ProductCode
parameters.description: The product code of the installed MSI.

parameters.name: InstalledApplication
parameters.description: The InstalledApplication object of the installed MSI.

parameters.name: ArgumentList
parameters.description: Overrides the default parameters specified in the config.psd1 file.

parameters.name: AdditionalArgumentList
parameters.description: Adds additional parameters to the default set specified in the config.psd1 file.

parameters.name: SecureArgumentList
parameters.description: Hides all parameters passed to the MSI or MSP file from the toolkit log file.

parameters.name: WorkingDirectory
parameters.description: Overrides the working directory. The working directory is set to the location of the MSI file.

parameters.name: Transforms
parameters.description: The name(s) of the transform file(s) to be applied to the MSI. The transform files should be in the same directory as the MSI file.

parameters.name: Patches
parameters.description: The name(s) of the patch (MSP) file(s) to be applied to the MSI for the "Install" action. The patch files should be in the same directory as the MSI file.

parameters.name: RunAsActiveUser
parameters.description: A RunAsActiveUser object to invoke the process as.

parameters.name: UseLinkedAdminToken
parameters.description: Use a user's linked administrative token while running the process under their context.

parameters.name: UseHighestAvailableToken
parameters.description: Use a user's linked administrative token if it's available while running the process under their context.

parameters.name: InheritEnvironmentVariables
parameters.description: Specifies whether the process running as a user should inherit the SYSTEM account's environment variables.

parameters.name: DenyUserTermination
parameters.description: Specifies that users cannot terminate the process started in their context. The user will still be able to terminate the process if they're an administrator, though.

parameters.name: UseUnelevatedToken
parameters.description: If the current process is elevated, starts the new process unelevated using the user's unelevated linked token.

parameters.name: ExpandEnvironmentVariables
parameters.description: Specifies whether to expand any Windows/DOS-style environment variables in the specified FilePath/ArgumentList.

parameters.name: LoggingOptions
parameters.description: Overrides the default logging options specified in the config.psd1 file.

parameters.name: LogFileName
parameters.description: Overrides the default log file name. The default log file name is generated from the MSI file name. If LogFileName does not end in .log, it will be automatically appended. For uninstallations, by default the product code is resolved to the DisplayName and version of the application.

parameters.name: RepairMode
parameters.description: Specifies the mode of repair. Choosing `Repair` will repair via `msiexec.exe /p` (which can trigger unsupressable reboots). Choosing `Reinstall` will reinstall by adding `REINSTALL=ALL REINSTALLMODE=omus` to the standard InstallParams.

parameters.name: RepairFromSource
parameters.description: Specifies whether we should repair from source. Also rewrites local cache.

parameters.name: SkipMSIAlreadyInstalledCheck
parameters.description: Skips the check to determine if the MSI is already installed on the system.

parameters.name: IncludeUpdatesAndHotfixes
parameters.description: Include matches against updates and hotfixes in results.

parameters.name: SuccessExitCodes
parameters.description: List of exit codes to be considered successful. Defaults to values set during ADTSession initialization, otherwise: 0

parameters.name: RebootExitCodes
parameters.description: List of exit codes to indicate a reboot is required. Defaults to values set during ADTSession initialization, otherwise: 1641, 3010

parameters.name: IgnoreExitCodes
parameters.description: List the exit codes to ignore or * to ignore all exit codes.

parameters.name: PriorityClass
parameters.description: Specifies priority class for the process. Options: Idle, Normal, High, AboveNormal, BelowNormal, RealTime.

parameters.name: ExitOnProcessFailure
parameters.description: Automatically closes the active deployment session via Close-ADTSession in the event the process exits with a non-success or non-ignored exit code.

parameters.name: NoDesktopRefresh
parameters.description: If specifies, doesn't refresh the desktop and environment after successful MSI installation.

parameters.name: NoWait
parameters.description: Immediately continue after executing the process.

parameters.name: PassThru
parameters.description: Returns ExitCode, StdOut, and StdErr output from the process. Note that a failed execution will only return an object if either `-ErrorAction` is set to `SilentlyContinue`/`Ignore`, or if `-IgnoreExitCodes`/`-SuccessExitCodes` are used.

examples:
Start-ADTMsiProcess -Action 'Install' -FilePath 'Adobe_FlashPlayer_11.2.202.233_x64_EN.msi'

Install an MSI.

Start-ADTMsiProcess -Action 'Install' -FilePath 'Adobe_FlashPlayer_11.2.202.233_x64_EN.msi' -Transforms 'Adobe_FlashPlayer_11.2.202.233_x64_EN_01.mst' -ArgumentList '/QN'

Install an MSI, applying a transform and overriding the default MSI toolkit parameters.

$ExecuteMSIResult = Start-ADTMsiProcess -Action 'Install' -FilePath 'Adobe_FlashPlayer_11.2.202.233_x64_EN.msi' -PassThru

Install an MSI and stores the result of the execution into a variable by using the -PassThru option.

$ExecuteMSIResult = Start-ADTMsiProcess -Action 'Install' -FilePath 'Adobe_FlashPlayer_11.2.202.233_x64_EN.msi' -AdditionalArgumentList 'ALLUSERS=1', 'SOMEPROPERTY=TRUE' -PassThru

Install an MSI and stores the result of the execution into a variable by using the -PassThru option, specifically taking advantage of our `-AdditionalArgumentList` array support to avoid escaped quote issues.

Start-ADTMsiProcess -Action 'Uninstall' -ProductCode '{26923b43-4d38-484f-9b9e-de460746276c}'

Uninstall an MSI using a product code.

Start-ADTMsiProcess -Action 'Patch' -FilePath 'Adobe_Reader_11.0.3_EN.msp'

Install an MSP.
functions.outputs: PSADT.Types.ProcessResult Returns an object with the results of the installation if -PassThru is specified. - ExitCode - StdOut - StdErr

It lets you open a file or a url and the Shell will figure out the program to open it with. The WorkingDirectory property behaves differently depending on the value of the UseShellExecute property. When UseShellExecute is true, the WorkingDirectory property specifies the location of the executable. When UseShellExecute is false, the WorkingDirectory property is not used to find the executable. Instead, it is used only by the process that is started and has meaning only within the context of the new process. If you set UseShellExecute to $true, there will be no available output from the process.

parameters.name: WaitForChildProcesses
parameters.description: Specifies whether the started process should be considered finished only when any child processes it spawns have finished also.

parameters.name: KillChildProcessesWithParent
parameters.description: Specifies whether any child processes started by the provided executable should be closed when the provided executable closes. This is handy for application installs that open web browsers and other programs that cannot be suppressed.

parameters.name: Timeout
parameters.description: How long to wait for the process before timing out.

parameters.name: TimeoutAction
parameters.description: What action to take on timeout. Follows ErrorAction if not specified.

parameters.name: NoTerminateOnTimeout
parameters.description: Indicates that the process should not be terminated on timeout. Only supported for GUI-based applications.

parameters.name: SuccessExitCodes
parameters.description: List of exit codes to be considered successful. Defaults to values set during ADTSession initialization, otherwise: 0

parameters.name: RebootExitCodes
parameters.description: List of exit codes to indicate a reboot is required. Defaults to values set during ADTSession initialization, otherwise: 1641, 3010

parameters.name: IgnoreExitCodes

parameters.name: ExitOnProcessFailure

Launch InstallShield "setup.exe" from the ".\Files" sub-directory.

Launch InstallShield "setup.exe" from the ".\Files\Bin" sub-directory.

Launch InstallShield "setup.exe" from the ".\Files" sub-directory and force log files to the logging folder.

Launch InstallShield "setup.exe" with embedded MSI and force log files to the logging folder.

$result = Start-ADTProcess -FilePath "setup.exe" -ArgumentList "-i -f `"$($adtSession.DirFiles)\licenseFile.lic`"" -CreateNoWindow -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -PassThru

Launch "setup.exe" with -PassThru so we can capture the exit code and stdout/stderr from the executable if it's a console application.

$result = Start-ADTProcess -FilePath cmd.exe -ArgumentList '/c', 'echo Testing stdout capture. & exit 0' -CreateNoWindow -PassThru

Launch cmd.exe to echo out a message to stdout, specifically taking advantage of our `-ArgumentList` array support to avoid escaped quote issues.
